trial_court: Senior Civil Judge and Principal JMFC, Tarikere, M.C No.10/2003
case_name: K Mallikarjuna vs H A Sudha Mallikarjuna
facts_of_case: Marriage was solemnised in 1999. Respondent withdrew from husband's company without just cause and refused to cohabit. Husband sought divorce under Section 13(1)(ib) of Hindu Marriage Act, 1955.

legal_principles.principle: A party seeking divorce must establish that the other party has deserted them for a continuous statutory period of two years.
legal_principles.held: The cause and consent of him has willfully deserted him for continuous statutory period of two years as required under Section 13(1)(i-b) of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955.

legal_principles.principle: A party seeking divorce must establish that the marriage is irretrievably broken and there is no possibility of reconciliation.
legal_principles.held: Absolutely there is no possibility of reconciliation of the marriage and the marriage is irretrievably broken

outcome.final_order: Marriage is totally dead and nothing is gained by trying to keep the parties tied for ever to a marriage that in fact has ceased to exist.

keywords: Latin Maxim: Nemo dat quod non habet
